feed.title: Unwrapping the Stack
feed.subtitle: A layer-by-layer examination of files, apps, browsers, operating systems, hardware, and identity — and what happens to each when intelligence becomes a system property.

entry.title: Files & Folders — the first abstraction that starts to break
entry.summary: The first abstraction that starts to break. What happens to cognitive scaffolding when the system starts to think.

entry.title: Apps — the container that outlived its contents
entry.summary: The container that outlived its contents. What happens to software packaging when intent is the interface.

entry.title: Browsers — the universal runtime hiding in plain sight
entry.summary: The universal runtime hiding in plain sight. What happens when the address bar and document model give way to agentic sessions.

entry.title: Operating Systems — the gatekeeper beneath every interface
entry.summary: The gatekeeper beneath every interface. What happens when the operating system mediates intent instead of syscalls.

entry.title: Hardware — the substrate where intelligence lands
entry.summary: Silicon, accelerators, edge and cloud. What happens when intelligence stops being a service you call and becomes a property of the machine itself.

entry.title: Identity — who is the user when the system acts?
entry.summary: Accounts, keys, personas, and delegation. Who is the user when agents act on their behalf — and what the whole stack looks like when intelligence is ambient.
